explain.say: Imagine you had a friend who remembers a world with no smartphones and no internet. You might already have one: a grandparent! Look at the timeline. This is Nani, a grandmother, born in 1958 in a village near Kolkata.

events.ask: What questions can I ask my grandparents?

explain.say: Elders are like living history books. Here are great questions to ask: what games did you play? What was school like? What was your first job? What did you eat? Which question would you ask first?

steps.label: Can you teach me?
steps.note: A recipe, a song or a craft.

explain.say: And the best one: can you teach me? A recipe, a song or a craft. Wonderful! Wow fact: Japan has a national holiday, Respect for the Aged Day, to honour older people. Ask an elder one question this week!

faq.q: What questions can I ask my grandparents?
faq.a: Try: What games did you play? What was school like? What was your first job? What did you eat? What has changed most since you were my age?
asks: What can I ask my grandma about her life?

faq.q: What was school like for grandparents?
faq.a: It depends where they grew up. Many wrote on slates or with ink pens, walked far to school, and had no computers. Ask yours: every story is different!
asks: Tell me about the Starts school

faq.a: They share love, stories, skills and family history. Many help look after grandchildren, and they remember things nobody else does.

faq.q: What if my grandparents live far away or have died?
faq.a: You can call, video chat or write letters. If they have died, you can ask your parents for their stories and look at old photos together. Other elders can be special too.
asks: My grandparents live in another country

faq.q: How can I help older people?
faq.a: Spend time with them, listen to their stories, help carry things, teach them a phone trick, and be patient if they move slowly.
asks: How can I be kind to elders?

facts: Japan celebrates Respect for the Aged Day (Keiro no Hi) on the third Monday of September as a national holiday.
In the USA, National Grandparents Day is the first Sunday after Labor Day in September.
